thread:
jess: quick proposal — add a lightweight routing hint header on embed requests so the router can pick size-aware lanes. thinking header name: `X-Embed-Frame` with values like `single`, `batched:N`, `large-bytes`. goal: fewer surprises from autosplitter + better telemetry for console cost estimates.

sri: curious — what's the exact contract? do we expect clients to set it, or our SDKs to infer and set it?

jess: SDKs set it when possible. server will treat it as advisory only, still validate payloads. plan: 1) header accepted, 2) router uses it to prefer capacity pools (small/fast vs wide-batch), 3) console shows estimated per-request unit cost and a suggestion if header missing.

mike: +1 for advisory. we need guardrails tho — malicious clients could lie and hammer small pools. can we attach a soft-tenant quota or score so router can override?

jess: yes — router combines header with observed size metrics and tenant history. header just nudges routing, not full policy.

tara: for console UX — we can add a tiny estimator next to the Embeds route page that shows: "expected unit cost" / "likely split?" based on sample payload. we can also surface a "why this route" tooltip that says header influenced route.

sri: telemetry ask: record `embed.frame_hint` tag + `embed.actual_frames` and `embed.split_reason` for every oversized request. need to decide sampling.

infra-bot: deploy check: make sure header parsing added to edge and to private control-plane. will add lint to edge for header length.

mike: also needs quota impact. if header says `batched:16` but actual items=1 huge text, we shouldn't bill as batched. telemetry must correlate requested vs actual to detect mismatch and feed into console alerts.

jess: agreed. billing always uses actual tokens/bytes. header only affects routing. we'll add a console flag to highlight tenants with repeated header mismatches.

sri: rollout plan idea: opt-in toggle on console per org. start with internal tenants + a beta cohort. collect: routing latency delta, split frequency, pool hotness, and mismatch rate.

tara: timeline? I can prototype the estimator widget if we have a telemetry schema by EOD Friday.

jess: prototype header parsing + router nudge by Wednesday, telemetry events schema tomorrow morning. tara — ping me if you need a sample API to hit.

mike: concern — how will this interact with our existing preflight/dim negotiation flow? we currently do preflight to decide splits based on per-item dims. header could bypass some preflight work and cause spurious routing.

jess: router will still call the preflight analyzer for any request above thresholds. header only shortcuts routing for small/obvious requests. low-risk path for <1KB small items.

sri: add one more event: `embed.routing_decision` with fields: reason=(header|preflight|fallback), chosen_pool, latency_estimate. we'll need to keep this sparse to control cardinality.

ops-bot: FYI — rolling this out will require a small update to the SDKs (js/py/go). ops automation can coordinate canary and feature flags.

mike: ok. for security: validate header against ASCII token regex, max length 64. no nested JSON in header.

jess: noted. I'll open the design PR with examples and a sample curl:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\n  -H "X-Embed-Frame: batched:8" \\n  -d '{"input": ["short one", "short two"]}'
```

tara: nice. also add console hint when header absent: "Try adding X-Embed-Frame for better performance hints" and a link to doc.

sri: final ask — let's add a nightly job to compute tenant-level mismatch rates and surface top offenders in console. that'll help platform teams reach out.

jess: solid. I'll draft the telemetry schema + rollout notes and tag you both. thanks all. :thumbsup:
